trigger: A reader calls discover_instructions or GET /api/v1/discover/instructions against a catalogue of up to 5000 definitions each near the 256 KiB schema cap (a Write holder plants them)
summary: Discovery canonicalised every definition on every request, uncached: measured about 5.6 ms and 2.2 MB RSS per near-cap definition (roughly 28 s CPU and an extra 11 GB at 5000 definitions); a realistic catalogue (279 definitions, 98,475 stored bytes) is negligible (0.12 s whole catalogue at -O0 on one host). Also raised by: cpp-safety, architect.
classification_rationale: no aggregate bound on a new per-request cost

summary: Aggregate canonicalisation budget kDiscoveryCanonicalBudgetBytes = 4 MiB (about 43x the shipped catalogue): a definition that would exceed it publishes input_schema null with the fixed token input_schema_budget_exceeded, per definition so a smaller later row can still fit, empty and {} rows exempt (215a19611). Refined in 4c5f826fd: over-cap legacy rows are rejected in O(1) and never charged, whitespace variants of {} are exempt. Re-reviewed by security-guardian (cannot be bypassed by many just-under-budget rows; no auth change), cpp-safety, cpp-expert, quality-engineer, consistency-auditor, dsl-engineer: closed. The raw per-request parse of every stored schema and the response size remain proportional to the catalogue (pre-existing, now documented accurately).

severity_native: SHOULD (architect, disagreeing with its own derived HIGH)
trigger: A legacy or data-layer row whose schema canonicalises but that prepare_param_validator refuses: pattern over the RE2 budget, default violating its constraints, non-numeric or inverted bounds, keyword on the wrong type
summary: Docs, header and tool description named only an uncompilable regex as the case where input_schema is non-null but execute answers 500; the real set is every rejection of the shared schema compiler plus the pattern budget and default checks. Recorded at the architect's derived band (I3 base HIGH, E6 not proven because legacy rows exist); fixed by making the text true, not by waiver. Also raised by: consistency-auditor, docs-writer, cpp-safety.
classification_rationale: incomplete enumeration of a published limit

summary: Limit widened to 'any stored schema prepare_param_validator refuses' in the header, rest-api.md, mcp.md, the tool description, the in-band catalog description and the OpenAPI entry (215a19611, 4c5f826fd); pinned by a unit case with five shapes canonicalise accepts and prepare refuses and by a route-level legacy-pattern test; re-reviewed by consistency-auditor, docs-writer, dsl-engineer: closed.

trigger: Docs-lint on a runner whose only PyYAML is the --user install; a PyPI outage hitting the REQUIRED 'CHANGELOG order' check
summary: The lint test spawned its child runs with python -I (which ignores the --user site where CI installs PyYAML), and the PyPI install had been added to the dependency-light required changelog-order job, making the file header false. Also raised by: quality-engineer, docs-writer.
classification_rationale: comment and design contradicted the wiring

summary: -I removed; the install and lint moved to their own definition-descriptions job with a corrected header comment (215a19611); changelog-order is byte-identical to origin/dev (build-ci verified); a timeout was added to the child runs (4c5f826fd). The new job is advisory until an owner adds it to the Protect Dev/Main rulesets (six required contexts today); enforcement is not lost because any PR touching definitions runs the meson docs suite on the three required platform legs.

summary: The ledger said no temp path or subprocess is added and called the Python lint read-only; the test adds a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory and subprocess.run calls (argv list, no shell), and later the budget accounting and a timeout.

C++-only qualifier, rows for the temp directory, the child process (with timeout), the budget and the CI job (62a5f5cce, 4c5f826fd); cpp-safety verified the rows against the code at 215a19611: complete.

summary: The instructions catalogue stays at version 1 after two additive required output fields, whereas discover_plugins bumped its version for an additive docs field.

Declined: the fields are additive (parameter_schema unchanged, no consumer keys on them), the plugins bump was a different change, and a bump would break clients pinning version 1 for no benefit. Rejected at NICE needs no adjudicator.
